chunks: And Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"There is no harm if the Muhrim (person in Ihram) catches fish and eats it fresh or salted, and provisions himself," Allah the Exalted said: 'Permitted to you is the game of the sea and its food as provision for you.'
He said: 'So let those who eat choose.'

And he said: 'The distinction between the two is: every bird that stays in the thickets, lays eggs on land, and hatches on land, it is from the game of the land; and whatever of the birds stays in the sea and hatches in the sea, it is from the game of the sea.'
The Sheikh (peace be upon him) said: 'If he kills many bees, he gives charity with a Mudd of food or a Mudd of dates.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (consecration) for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.صَيْدُ الْبَحْرِ: Game of the sea (fish and sea creatures)
key_terms.صَيْدُ الْبَرِّ: Game of the land (terrestrial animals and birds)
key_terms.مُدٍّ: A specific unit of volume measurement for charity

ai.seo_question: What can a person in Ihram eat from the sea according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, clarifying the distinction between sea game (which is exempt from Ihram restrictions) and land game based on the habitat of egg-laying and hatching. The hadith further specifies that killing bees incurs a fidya (expiation) of one mud of food or dates, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Imams regarding minor violations during pilgrimage.
